news.title: NewsBusters Podcast: Democrat Candidates Can Do No Wrong
news.description: NewsBusters Podcast: Democrat Candidates Can Do No Wrong As we watch TV news during the midterm season, what we've mostly noticed is that there's not much news about candidates -- just some general tilt against Trump's bad approval ratings. But Democrats get a pass, and Republican flubs are news. So Sen. Eric Schmitt getting his facts wrong in a question to former special counsel Jack Smith is the only story of that hearing. There was no time to consider that Smith was an out-of-control partisan trying to make sure Trump didn't get re-elected in 2024. GOP Senate candidate Ken Paxton caught on audio by The New York Times complaining Trump's midterm convention hurt him politically becomes a TV story. Because good news for Democrats is what is considered "newsworthy." They just do not care how it makes them look like DNC Media. NewsBusters Associate Editor Nick Fondacaro and Senior Research Analyst Bill D'Agostino joined the show. The media ignored Maine Democrat Troy Jackson this week having to apologize after claiming “It’s unfortunate that there are people here in Maine that don’t like to use that term [genocide] only because they’re Jewish and what that means to them with the Holocaust,” Jackson told News Center Maine about Israel. “It fits that description, and it is [a genocide].” Nick explained all the drama over The View co-host Sunny Hostin boasting that she was a holdout juror on behalf of the "Butcher of Tompkins Square Park," who killed someone and then cooked their corpse and fed it to homeless people. She wanted to explain how passionately she favors an insanity defense. As network shows begin returning to television for the fall season, CBS’s liberal, TDS-laden “Sitcom King” Chuck Lorre, who we’ve covered extensively, has once again taken shots at President Trump as a “bloated orange piece of” excrement who he wishes would die of a heart attack on the toilet, and insulted First Lady Melania Trump as a “surgically enhanced, cold-hearted Yugoslavian escort who clearly hates her husband. Finally, NBC's Saturday Night Live loves the socialist mayor of New York so much that they turned President Trump into a desperate Mamdani fan. The fake president told the fake mayor: “I just love hanging out with you. We’re like one of those unlikely animal friendships, like when a tiger gets together with a baby goat. When I see stuff like that, I want to text it to you and say, this could be us!” We even get this fake gush: “You're in most of my dreams. I call you Mam-dreamy. Pick me, choose me, love me!” Enjoy the show below. news.title: ABC Continues to Milk Paxton Gaffe While Pushing Poll DOOM
news.description: ABC Continues to Milk Paxton Gaffe While Pushing Poll DOOM For a second consecutive evening Disney-owned ABC World News Tonight, the most Trump-deranged of the Elitist Media evening newscasts, has elected to run a news item highlighting Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton’s remarks complaining on the GOP Midterm Convention. For the second consecutive night, ABC pushed “Republicans in Disarray” and polling DOOM!!11!! Watch the report in its entirety as aired on ABC World News Tonight on Thursday, October 1st, 2026: WATCH: For a second consecutive day, @ABCWorldNews milks the Paxton post-convention remarks and pushes polling DOOM while omitting Troy Jackson's brutal "genocide" remarks DAVID MUIR: This evening, the midterm election of course, now 33 days away. And President Trump, amid some… pic.twitter.com/3eSYK8kt9C — Jorge Bonilla (@BonillaJL) October 2, 2026 DAVID MUIR: This evening, the midterm election of course, now 33 days away. And President Trump, amid some of his lowest poll numbers on record and deep concern over inflation, the president now traveling to five deep red states. Here's Rachel Scott tonight. RACHEL SCOTT: Tonight, President Trump in Texas, where one of the fiercest Senate races could decide control of Congress. He arrived with a new poll showing his national approval rating at 31%, a record low. The president won Texas handily, but now polls in the Senate race show the Democrat, James Talarico, leading Republican Ken Paxton. After the president held his midterm convention in Dallas, The New York Times obtained audio of Paxton complaining it hurt his campaign. KEN PAXTON: When we did that convention, it dropped our numbers. Everybody’s numbers dropped. Right now, yeah, not good. SCOTT: Today in Texas, Trump praising Paxton. DONALD TRUMP: Ken Paxton was at my side more than anybody. And I have to always remember that because he could be a pain in the ass sometimes, I'll be honest. SCOTT: Other Republicans keeping the president at arm's length. Still, President Trump today giving himself a grade A-plus. TRUMP: I give us an A-plus on the government, on economics, on everything. Look at inflation. I inherited the worst inflation in history under Biden, worst in history. And now it's great. SCOTT: But the reality is inflation has jumped since Trump took office from 2.8% to 3.4%. 80% of Americans disapprove of how he's handling it. And today, Vice President JD Vance with a very different message from the president, urging Republicans to not, quote, “ignore people's concerns.” JD VANCE: Listen to people who are upset with the state of the economy. If we don't listen to people, we will turn into the very thing that we hate. SCOTT: This is the president's first major midterm campaign swing. He'll be here in Oklahoma tonight. Then over the next few days, we'll see him in Alabama, Ohio and Nebraska, all states he has won before as he tries to energize his core supporters to turn out to the polls. David. MUIR: Rachel Scott live with us tonight. Rachel, thanks. The report, a rehash of the previous evening’s slop , obviously serves little purpose except to assist Democrat Senate candidate James Talarico and discourage Republicans from voting in the midterm. This explains the steady drumbeat of consistently citing negative poll numbers for President Trump. So devoted to this mission is ABC that they’ve broadly stopped reporting on some of the other Senate races that previously dominated coverage, such as Michigan and Maine. Speaking of Maine, the networks all continue to omit Democrat Senate candidate Troy Jackson’s comments on the Holocaust. Per NBC News Center Maine : Maine Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Troy Jackson is apologizing for comments he made this week in a NEWS CENTER Maine candidate profile interview about Israeli “genocide” in Gaza. In reiterating his view that that the three-year-old Israel-Gaza war “is a genocide,” Jackson said in the interview, “There are people here in Maine that don't like to use that term only because, you know, they're Jewish and, you know, what that means to them with the Holocaust.” Jackson has since apologized for those remarks. An apology would have extended the news cycle into the weekend had a Republican proffered similar remarks. Instead, it is all swept under the rug. Between omitting the Jackson scandal while continuing to flog the Paxton remarks, ABC demonstrates why their news content is under scrutiny.
